Package neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.olga

Class SyntheticWellTrajectory

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.fielddevelopment.olga.SyntheticWellTrajectory
public final class SyntheticWellTrajectory extends Object
Generates a synthetic (not a specific well's real) wellbore deviation trajectory -- (MD, TVD) station arrays -- for use when no real Prosper model, SMDA record, or other real trajectory source exists for a well, interpolated from a caller-supplied, depth-dependent statistics basis rather than a single generic textbook default or a bare vertical pipe.

Why this exists

A well's wellbore geometry materially affects an OLGA transient multiphase result (slugging, terrain-induced liquid accumulation are deviation-sensitive), so assuming a purely vertical well when no real survey exists is not a neutral simplification -- it can be a materially worse approximation than a realistic deviated profile. Real well populations typically show build rate and kickoff depth varying materially with total depth, so a single fixed "representative" well shape is usually a poor match for the real population; this class instead interpolates a depth-dependent build rate/kickoff-point from three depth tiers (shallow/medium/deep) that the caller supplies, rather than hardcoding one fixed shape or any field-derived numbers in this public library itself.

Data governance -- no statistics are embedded in this class

This class deliberately ships with no default SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics basis and no embedded field/well data. neqsim is a public, open-source repository; the depth-tier statistics a real caller would use (derived from a real well population) may be governed by that organization's own data-handling rules and must not be published here. Every caller MUST construct and supply its own SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics (three SyntheticWellTrajectory.DepthTier instances plus a default max inclination, optionally with its own basisDescription provenance string) from whatever internally governed data source it has rights to use -- see this class's own SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics and SyntheticWellTrajectory.DepthTier Javadoc. A small, clearly-labeled example basis for experimentation is provided only in this class's own unit tests (round, invented numbers -- not derived from any real well).

What this is NOT

  • NOT a real well's actual trajectory. Every genkey or report built from this class's output MUST disclose that plainly -- see syntheticTrajectoryWarning(Result), never silently presented as real geometry.
  • NOT a substitute for a real planned/as-drilled trajectory (SMDA, a real Prosper deviation survey, or a real drilling-engineering well-planning tool) when one is available. Always prefer real data; use this class only when no real trajectory source exists for the well in question.
  • NOT a full well-planning tool. It builds a simple, standard "build and hold" (or "build only", when the target is reached before completing the full build) analytic circular-arc profile -- it does not model doglegs, S-shaped profiles, or multi-target wells.

Method

Standard "radius of curvature" analytic circular-arc geometry (unit-weight textbook directional-drilling convention): 

     bRadPerM = radians(buildRateDegPer30m) / 30    // curvature
     radiusM  = 1 / bRadPerM                          // radius (m)
     md(inc)  = kopMd + radiusM * inc                 // along the arc
     tvd(inc) = kopMd + radiusM * sin(inc)             // along the arc

applied in up to three sections: a vertical section (0 to KOP, where MD == TVD), a build section (circular arc from 0 to either the statistics basis's typical max inclination or a lower inclination if the target TVD is reached first), and -- only if the target TVD has NOT yet been reached at the end of the full build -- a straight tangent/hold section at constant inclination for the remaining TVD. An optional reservoir-contact length then extends the well further, at the terminal inclination, WITHOUT requiring further net TVD gain -- this mirrors a pattern commonly observed when characterizing a real well population: the full build arc alone often already reaches a depth tier's own approximate target TVD well before exhausting that tier's own typical max inclination, meaning a real well's extra MD beyond the build arc is often best modeled as a reservoir-contact/lateral section, not as additional vertical-depth-seeking tangent length.

    Description
    private static final double
    LONG_TANGENT_WARNING_RATIO
    A tangent/hold section longer than this, relative to the target TVD itself, is flagged as an explicit warning rather than silently returned -- it usually means the max-inclination/build-rate combination in use is a poor fit for this particular target TVD, not a normal result.
    private static final double
    MAX_SAFE_INCLINATION_DEG
    Inclination is capped below 90 degrees to keep cos(inclination) bounded away from zero in the tangent-section formula (md = remainingTvd / cos(inclination)) -- an uncapped 90 degrees (or a caller-supplied value at or above it) would make that division blow up or divide by zero. 89.0 degrees still represents an effectively horizontal hold section (over 99.98% of unit length is still horizontal travel) while keeping the formula numerically well-behaved.
    static final String
    SYNTHETIC_TRAJECTORY_WARNING_PREFIX
    Warning prefix mirroring well-inflow-pi's own [CHOKE WARNING]/[GEOMETRY WARNING] convention.

    • generateSyntheticTrajectory

      public static SyntheticWellTrajectory.Result generateSyntheticTrajectory(double targetTvdMetre, SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics statistics)
      Generate a synthetic (MD, TVD) wellbore trajectory for a given target TVD, with no reservoir-contact extension and the statistics basis's own default max inclination. See generateSyntheticTrajectory(double, double, Double, int, Statistics) for the full set of options.
      Parameters:
      targetTvdMetre - target true vertical depth (m) the well must reach, must be positive
      statistics - the depth-tier statistics basis to interpolate against -- every caller must supply its own; see this class's own "Data governance" Javadoc section
      Returns:
      the generated trajectory
      Throws:
      SyntheticWellTrajectory.SyntheticTrajectoryException - if targetTvdMetre is not positive

    • generateSyntheticTrajectory

      public static SyntheticWellTrajectory.Result generateSyntheticTrajectory(double targetTvdMetre, double reservoirContactLengthMetre, Double maxInclinationDegOverride, int buildSectionNumStations, SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics statistics)
      Generate a synthetic (MD, TVD) wellbore trajectory for a given target TVD, grounded in a caller-supplied depth-tier statistics basis -- see this class's own Javadoc for the full method and rationale.
      Parameters:
      targetTvdMetre - target true vertical depth (m) the well must reach (e.g. the reservoir datum depth); must be positive
      reservoirContactLengthMetre - optional additional MD (m) to extend the well beyond reaching targetTvdMetre, at the terminal inclination, representing a reservoir-contact/lateral section. Zero means stop exactly at targetTvdMetre. This is a SEPARATE concern from reaching targetTvdMetre itself -- see this class's own Javadoc for the reasoning. Must be zero or greater.
      maxInclinationDegOverride - optional override for the maximum build inclination (degrees); null defaults to statistics's own SyntheticWellTrajectory.Statistics.defaultMaxInclinationDeg. Capped at MAX_SAFE_INCLINATION_DEG regardless of the value given.
      buildSectionNumStations - number of (MD, TVD) stations to emit across the build section (including both endpoints, minimum 2). Higher values give a smoother arc at the cost of a larger array.
      statistics - the depth-tier statistics basis to interpolate against. This class ships with no built-in default -- every caller must supply its own, derived from whatever internally governed data source it has rights to use (production use), or a small fixture (testing); see this class's own "Data governance" Javadoc section and the ported Python module's own statistics= parameter, which this mirrors.
      Returns:
      the generated trajectory. May be a purely vertical profile (MD == TVD throughout, with an explanatory warning in SyntheticWellTrajectory.Result.warnings) rather than a curved one, if targetTvdMetre is shallower than (or equal to) the depth tier's own interpolated kickoff-point depth -- that is the physically correct result in that case, not an error; always inspect SyntheticWellTrajectory.Result.warnings rather than assuming a curved profile.
      Throws:
      SyntheticWellTrajectory.SyntheticTrajectoryException - if targetTvdMetre is not positive, or reservoirContactLengthMetre is negative

    • syntheticTrajectoryWarning

      public static String syntheticTrajectoryWarning(SyntheticWellTrajectory.Result result)
      Return the single, canonical warning string for a generated synthetic trajectory, suitable for a genkey header comment or a warnings collector -- mirrors well-inflow-pi's own [CHOKE WARNING]/ [GEOMETRY WARNING] convention.
      Parameters:
      result - the result from any generateSyntheticTrajectory(...) overload
      Returns:
      a single warning string, always non-empty regardless of whether result.warnings itself is empty -- a synthetic trajectory is always worth disclosing, not only when something unusual happened during its generation

    • buildArcStations

      private static double[][] buildArcStations(double kopMd, double radiusM, double incTargetRad, int numStations)
      Discretize a circular-arc build section into (MD, TVD) station pairs, from inclination 0 (at kopMd) to incTargetRad.
      Parameters:
      kopMd - MD (and TVD) at the start of the build section
      radiusM - radius of curvature (m), i.e. 1 / bRadPerM
      incTargetRad - inclination (radians) to build to
      numStations - number of stations to emit, including both endpoints (minimum 2)
      Returns:
      a 2-row array: row 0 is MD values, row 1 is TVD values
